result.reasoning:
REFUTED on five independent grounds; I could not produce a single wrong number.

1) Self-declared non-numeric, and therefore out of the reportable class. The reporter writes "Not a numeric defect ... this is a documentation completeness gap only" and records "0 mismatches in every run" in their own verification. The review mandate is restricted to defects that change a number or a conclusion, with comments/wording excluded. A docstring phrasing gap whose implementation is verified exact cannot move the selection metric (long-leg net excess, 10% equal-weight book, 15bp) by any amount.

2) Independent reproduction found 0 mismatches, including in the exact regime where the ambiguity is reachable. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/ops4_bucket_doc/repro.py rebuilds cs_bucket_demean and cs_bucket_zscore from scratch (pct-rank with value-then-original-index tiebreak, ceil(r/n*10) clamped to 1..10, population std + EPS=1e-9, NaN when bucket n<2) and compares against the implementation over 13 scenarios x 2 dtypes = 26 runs: heavy ties (3 distinct x values) at S in {23,10,9,3,2,1}, constant x (one tie block spanning the whole cross-section), ties + 30% NaN scatter, continuous no-tie x, scales 1e9/1e16/1e-9, all-NaN x. Result: demean_mismatch=0 and zscore_mismatch=0 in all 26, total 0.

3) The operator's output cannot depend on which reading a caller assumes — that is the structural reason this can never become numeric. Output is deterministic (0 mismatches on repeat) and matches the rank+index reading exactly (0) while differing from the value-quantile reading (80 cells on a 4x20 heavy-tie panel). The 80 disagreeing cells are between two *hypothetical references*, not between the code and anything; the code produces the rank-cut answer regardless of what a reader believed. Under continuous x the two readings coincide exactly (0 mismatches), so the ambiguity is only even reachable under exact ties.

4) The finding's own premise — "read in isolation, a caller can't tell" — is factually wrong at the cited lines. ops_ext.py:407 (inside cs_bucket_demean's docstring) names the sibling: "Keeps y's units and magnitude (``cs_bucket_rank`` throws them away)". ops_ext.py:425 (cs_bucket_zscore's docstring) opens "As ``cs_bucket_demean`` but divided by ...". Both docstrings therefore carry an explicit pointer along the chain zscore -> demean -> cs_bucket_rank, and cs_bucket_rank:233 states "(deciles of x by rank; NaN where either is missing)". There is no reading path on which the clause is unreachable; the finding asserts an isolation that the source text does not have.

5) The new_operators.md half is answered by that file's own stated authority rule, and no second implementation exists. /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/docs/new_operators.md line 7 says in bold: the definition of every operator is governed by the docstring and code in ops_ext.py, not by the table or the name. A table row that defers to the code by design is not an incompleteness. And the only route from a doc ambiguity to a changed number — a second, value-quantile implementation of x-decile membership somewhere — does not exist: `_buckets` (ops_ext.py:400) has exactly two call sites, lines 413 and 429, i.e. the two operators under review; nothing in partura/ cuts x into deciles by value quantile. steer.py:380-401 (`_bucket` / `_bucket_rank`) is a separate liquidity-bucket reward path and is itself rank-based (stable argsort then floor(pos/cnt*n)), so it does not contradict the rank reading either.

6) Additionally, the tie hazard the finding speculates a reader would miss is already written down in the project's own handoff record: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/handoff/TOOLING.md:114 names cs_bucket_rank AND cs_bucket_demean together, states that `_pct_rank`'s tie-break slices a large tie block arbitrarily across several deciles, and records the research decision taken because of it (hypo3's T group switched to cs_first_low20 instead of bucketing). The requesting document for the operator (handoff/F110_ret_fair_log/agents/synth_a4f321cb016b5ff04.md:1807) also specifies "x 的十分位按秩划分". The knowledge is present in the repo, so even the documentation claim is overstated.

Aside, not part of this verdict and already covered by TOOLING.md:114: bucket membership under heavy ties in x does depend on column (stock) order, and the author added an explicit 1e-4 rank tiebreak in cs_bucket_rank (ops_ext.py:247-249) with the comment "so no decile book hangs on symbol order" while demean/zscore have no analogous mitigation. That is a different question from the reported finding (which is purely about docstring wording) and is already recorded in the handoff notes, so I am not converting it into a confirmation here.

No files under /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura or /Users/wxy/Desktop/AlphaCube were modified; the only file written is the scratch script under tmp/review/verify/.
